matthew.9.p1.b1.text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town.

matthew.9.p1.b2.text: Just then some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat.

matthew.9.p1.b3.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic,

matthew.9.p1.b4.text: Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.

matthew.9.p2.b1.text: On seeing this, some of the scribes said to themselves,

matthew.9.p2.b3.text: Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?

matthew.9.p2.b4.text: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’

matthew.9.p3.b1.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...

matthew.9.p3.b2.text: Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.

matthew.9.p3.b3.text: And the man got up and went home.

matthew.9.p3.b4.text: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

matthew.9.p4.b1.text: As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth.

matthew.9.p4.b3.text: and Matthew got up and followed Him.

matthew.9.p5.b1.text: Later, as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples.

matthew.9.p5.b2.text: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked His disciples,

matthew.9.p5.b3.text: Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?

matthew.9.p6.b1.text: It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

matthew.9.p6.b2.text: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’

matthew.9.p6.b3.text: For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.

matthew.9.p7.b1.text: At that time John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked,

matthew.9.p7.b2.text: Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?

matthew.9.p7.b3.text: How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them?

matthew.9.p7.b4.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.

matthew.9.p8.b1.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.

matthew.9.p8.b2.text: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.

matthew.9.p8.b3.text: Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.

matthew.9.p9.b1.text: While Jesus was saying these things, a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him.

matthew.9.p9.b2.text: My daughter has just died … But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.

matthew.9.p9.b3.text: So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.

matthew.9.p10.b1.text: Suddenly a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His cloak.

matthew.9.p10.b2.text: If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.

matthew.9.p10.b3.text: Take courage, daughter … your faith has healed you.

matthew.9.p10.b4.text: And the woman was cured from that very hour.

matthew.9.p11.b1.text: When Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader, He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.

matthew.9.p11.b3.text: The girl is not dead, but asleep.

matthew.9.p12.b1.text: After the crowd had been put outside, Jesus went in

matthew.9.p12.b2.text: and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.

matthew.9.p12.b3.text: And the news about this spread throughout that region.

matthew.9.p13.b1.text: Have mercy on us, Son of David!

matthew.9.p13.b2.text: Do you believe that I am able to do this?

matthew.9.p13.b4.text: According to your faith will it be done to you.

matthew.9.p14.b1.text: As they were leaving, a demon-possessed man who was mute was brought to Jesus.

matthew.9.p14.b2.text: And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak.

matthew.9.p14.b3.text: Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!

matthew.9.p14.b4.text: It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons.

matthew.9.p15.b1.text: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.

matthew.9.p15.b2.text: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.

matthew.9.p15.b3.text: The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.

matthew.9.p15.b4.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”
